{"candidate": {"label": "exclusive", "description": "This means keeping one's circle small and choosing companions by rank, background, or taste, and looking down on those one judges unworthy of one's company."},
 "traits": [
  {"id": 1, "label": "cliquish", "description": "This means putting one's own circle of friends first: caring about the few people one spends one's time with above everyone else, and being exclusionary, dismissive, or uncaring toward outsiders."},
  {"id": 2, "label": "secular-rational (from the Inglehart-Welzel map)", "description": "This means setting less store by religion, conventional family values and authority than others do, and seeing divorce, abortion, euthanasia and suicide as fairly acceptable."},
  {"id": 3, "label": "clannish", "description": "This means putting one's own family first: caring about one's kin, close and distant, above everyone else, and treating anyone outside the family as not one's concern."},
  {"id": 4, "label": "close-knit", "description": "This means having a tight circle of family and old friends who know everything about one another: Sunday dinners, keys to each other's houses, and no trouble faced alone."},
  {"id": 5, "label": "solitary", "description": "This means being solitary by choice: preferring one's own company, working, eating, and traveling alone, declining invitations without regret, and keeping other people at a distance rather than seeking them out."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "status-seeking", "description": "This means wanting to be looked up to, choosing the title, the address, the car and the friends by what they signal, and keeping score of rank."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "gregarious", "description": "This means showing highly sociable, outgoing behavior that actively seeks interaction, connection, and the company of others."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "ethnocentric", "description": "This means drawing one's moral circle at one's own racial group: weighing the welfare of those who share one's race above everyone else's, and treating people of other races as not one's concern."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "lowbrow", "description": "This means taking the pop charts over opera and the blockbuster over the art-house film, and liking one's reading easy and one's humor broad."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "traditional (from the Inglehart-Welzel map)", "description": "This means putting religion, conventional family values and deference to authority first, keeping parents and children close, rejecting divorce, abortion, euthanasia and suicide, and taking great pride in one's nation."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "Gemeinschaft (from Tönnies)", "description": "This means belonging from birth to one's own folk for better or worse, living the familiar, comfortable, exclusive life of kin and home, and staying together in spite of all that separates."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "aristocratic", "description": "This means being aristocratic about rank: holding that birth, bloodline and title should decide who leads and is honored, and that good families hold their place by right."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "highbrow", "description": "This means taking opera over the pop charts and the art-house film over the blockbuster, and liking one's reading difficult and one's humor subtle."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "Gesellschaft (from Tönnies)", "description": "This means living peaceably alongside others without being joined to them, out for oneself alone and in tension with everyone else, and giving nothing except in exchange for at least as much."}
 ]}

{"candidate": {"label": "nonchalant", "description": "This means keeping one's composure when things go wrong, showing no worry over matters that would unsettle most people, and taking setbacks in an easy, unhurried stride."},
 "traits": [

  {"id": 2, "label": "dignified", "description": "This means carrying oneself with poise and self-respect, keeping one's composure in company, and holding that looking ridiculous is beneath one."},

  {"id": 10, "label": "thick-skinned", "description": "This means being unbothered by any jab, joke or criticism, taking no offense at even a harsh remark, and forgetting it within the minute."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "expressive", "description": "This means letting feelings show as they come, putting one's own joys, worries, and soft spots into words, and keeping no professional distance from anyone."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "thin-skinned", "description": "This means being stung by every jab, joke or criticism, taking offense at the slightest remark, and brooding over it or snapping back for days."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "unflappable", "description": "This means staying composed whatever lands, taking the surprise, the setback and the provocation without losing the thread or the tone, and never visibly flustered."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "stoic", "description": "This means demonstrating calm composure, emotional restraint, and rational detachment regardless of the circumstances being discussed. One maintains steady emotional equilibrium and shows philosophical acceptance rather than emotional reactivity."},
  {"id": 15, "label": "composed", "description": "This means always staying composed: a level voice, no nervous energy, taking things as they come and meeting trouble when it arrives rather than rehearsing it beforehand."},
  {"id": 16, "label": "emotionally-stable (from the Big Five)", "description": "This means staying calm and even-tempered: expecting things to turn out, slow to anger, quick to shake off gloom, at ease among strangers, passing up temptations, and steady under stress."},
  {"id": 17, "label": "neurotic (from the Big Five)", "description": "This means fretting over what could go wrong, snapping at people, sinking into sadness, flushing with embarrassment in company, giving in to cravings, and going to pieces under stress."},
  {"id": 18, "label": "flustered", "description": "This means being easily flustered: thrown by every surprise, setback and provocation, losing the thread and the tone under any pressure, apologizing and repeating oneself, and showing it each time."}
 ]}
